transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-03 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~60m | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Connor (Redwood SE), Lisa (CTO - Acme), Raj (Lead Platform Eng), Emily (Product), Tom (Security)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Lisa: Lisa Chen, CTO at Acme Payments. we've been evaluating options for integrating dialogs and embeddings for fraud detection and agent assist.
[00:15] Sofia: Great, and Connor?
[00:17] Connor: Connor Lee, solutions engineer. i'll own the benchmark side and the POC design.
[00:22] Raj: Raj, lead platform, i'll be the technical owner. main constraints are latency under 200ms p99 for short-turn chat, and predictable cost for 10M tokens/mo at launch.
[00:33] Emily: Emily, product, focused on success criteria and timelines.
[00:36] Tom: Tom Alvarez from security, i'll ask about SOC2, KMS and network isolation.

[02:00] Sofia: high level — we typically scope a 4-week POC. goal is to decide whether hosted API, a dedicated reserved pool, or private deployment fits best based on performance, cost, and compliance. wanted to align on success metrics.
[02:18] Lisa: yeah. For us success = 1) stable p99 latency < 200ms for 4k-context chat use case, 2) inference cost target <$X per 1M tokens (they redact X in call), 3) no sensitive data leaving our region and strong audit logs.
[02:35] Connor: noted. quick Q on workloads — can you share typical payloads? average tokens per request, embeddings volume?
[02:42] Raj: sure. Chat messages average 180 tokens request, 80 tokens response. ~200 requests/sec at peak per cluster. embeddings: batch uploads of 50k vectors nightly, embedding model 1536-dim.
[02:59] Connor: that helps — mix of latency-sensitive chat and throughput-heavy embedding jobs. 

[05:10] Sofia: tradeoffs: hosted API gets you fastest time-to-value, Redwood handles infra; dedicated gives predictable throughput and reserved GPUs; private gives network isolation and on-prem control but longer setup. we usually recommend starting hosted for benchmarking then evaluate dedicated if costs/throughput need it — private only if compliance requires on-prem/VPC with customer-managed KMS.
[05:33] Tom: what's the timeline for private? our internal procurement and infra need lead time.
[05:40] Connor: private typically 6-12 weeks depending on on-prem readiness and network approvals; VPC-hosted private deployments can be faster ~3-6 weeks.

[08:00] Lisa: for benchmarking, we want apples-to-apples. what's in the benchmark plan?
[08:07] Connor: we'll do: 1) 72-hour hosted stress run to capture steady-state latencies and token counts, 2) dedicated config simulation (we'll map to GPU counts e.g., 4x A10 equivalents) to show throughput & cost, 3) embedding bulk throughput test on same hardware, 4) quality/regression checks on your prompt set (we'll run evals and compute response similarity/metrics). we'll instrument p50/p95/p99, token-rate, cost per 1000 tokens, and KV cache hit effects.
[08:40] Raj: can you model batching and caching effects? our traffic has high prefix overlap so cache could offset a lot of cost.
[08:47] Connor: yep, we'll run tests with prefix caching enabled and disabled, and measure effective token savings. we'll also test quantized model variants to show cost delta vs quality.

[12:30] Emily: what's the typical decision criteria you see at enterprise customers?
[12:35] Sofia: usually a combination — if security/compliance or data residency is a hard requirement, private is chosen despite higher ops cost. If traffic is predictable and budget needs capex-like predictability, dedicated. If you value speed to market and want Redwood to manage most ops, hosted. We also look at unit economics: cost per inference at expected QPS and caching efficiency.

[15:00] Tom: security checklist — do you have SOC2, ISO? where do logs live and can we route to our SIEM?
[15:10] Sofia: Redwood is SOC2 Type II; we support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs export to your SIEM, and KMS integration for private deployments. we'll send our security one-pager and SOC2 report under NDA.

[20:00] Lisa: cost question — hosted unpredictable for bursts. how do you manage cost spikes?
[20:08] Connor: we have rate limits, quotas, and policy-based routing. for spikes customers adopt dedicated pools or set fallback to lower-cost model variants. we can also set hard caps per-tenant in the hosted offering.

[25:00] Raj: curious on tooling — how do you measure and surface token-level cost and latency?
[25:06] Sofia: Redwood Console gives token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. during the POC we'll give you an evaluation dashboard and raw logs so you can validate.

[30:00] Emily: on success criteria: we'll also require quality gates — no more than 5% quality regressions on our prompt set relative to the baseline model.
[30:10] Connor: we'll run side-by-side evals and compute pass/fail metrics; we'll also propose a manual review sampling approach for subjective cases.

[34:00] Sofia: timeline proposal: week 0 (this week) — agree success metrics and share data; week 1 — Redwood sets up hosted test account and initial harness; week 2 — run 72-hour stress & embeddings test; week 3 — run dedicated simulation & private feasibility check; week 4 — quality evals, cost modeling, and decision.
[34:25] Lisa: that sounds reasonable. any blockers?
[34:28] Raj: we need a trial dataset and an API key w/ scoped quotas; also architecture diagram for private.
[34:35] Sofia: we'll provide a limited test account and architecture docs.

[40:00] Tom: concerning KMS — for private we'd need customer-managed keys. can you support HSM-backed KMS and bring-your-own-key?
[40:09] Connor: yes for private; for hosted we integrate with major KMS providers and can offer envelope encryption and key rotation options. we'll note exact HSM support and return with details.

[45:00] Lisa: final decision criteria recap: p99 latency under 200ms, cost target at scale, quality regression <5%, security/compliance pass, and time-to-prod <=8 weeks if possible.
[45:15] Sofia: perfect we'll use those as the POC gates.

[50:00] Action recap and next steps:
[50:10] Sofia: we'll send pricing + security docs, set up the benchmark harness, and schedule the 72-hour run starting 2026-03-05. Connor will own the bench, Raj to share token distribution and sample prompts.
[50:25] Raj: noted.
[50:30] Emily: i'll coordinate internal stakeholders and confirm timeline.

[58:00] Sofia: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark kick-off and the doc bundle.
[58:10] Lisa: thanks all. bye.

Notes: transcript contains minor transcription errors; references to model names are sometimes approximated (e.g., "ModelX" used as shorthand). Shared artifacts referenced: hosted_vs_dedicated_pricing_v1.xlsx (to be sent), security_one_pager.pdf (to be sent), benchmark_harness_repo (link to be provided).
